content:
Last week, Apple filed a lawsuit against OpenAI, accusing its former employees of stealing trade secrets "for the benefit of OpenAI."

It is reported that Apple directly contacted several former employees currently working at OpenAI during the process.

According to the Financial Times, Apple has issued preservation orders to approximately 40 former employees.

A preservation order is a formal written notice sent to an individual or organization requiring them to preserve documents, records, and other evidence that may be relevant to a legal dispute. Such notices typically specify in detail the items that should be preserved.

This move stems from Apple's suspicion that the theft of trade secrets may extend beyond the scope identified when the lawsuit was first filed last week.

It is worth noting that Apple's lawsuit names OpenAI and io Products, along with former Apple employees Chang Liu and Tang Tan, as defendants.
